card.title: Test the Impossible Claim
card.instruction: Get someone else to take the first practical step that could prove the bizarre claim true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This tap gives you whatever you ask for. Ask for tea while I hold a cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're not using my good china for that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll hold a saucepan. You ask.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ask, but I'm not tasting anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask for a biscuit instead. If one comes out, we won't need your tongue as equipment.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 assigns B the magical request; A3 preserves that role with another vessel and A5 changes the requested output to observable food.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 china objection prompts A3 saucepan; B4 refusal to taste prompts A5 biscuit instead of tea.

relationship.evidence: B2 protects property and B4 bodily choice, while agreeing to ask, plausibly shaping a bounded test.

heightening.evidence: B4 rejects a verification method; A5 redesigns the output so B can initiate proof without tasting.
